3D opening title crawl

I wanted to know if one ElementGL WebGL 2 canvas could project a live editable HTML article onto a receding 3D cinema crawl over a starfield, fade far lines cleanly into space, and keep tilted buttons and inputs clickable with updateElementGeometry().

The live DOM strikes back

It is a period of GPU experimentation. Rebel <canvas> nodes striking from a layoutsubtree have won their first victory against static pixel screenshots.

Show the code ElementGL mipmapped upload, 3D perspective crawl shader, projective DOMMatrix and 2D trapezoid fallback
  1. The live drawable crawl article. One <article drawable> holds cinema-yellow semantic HTML, an editable <input>, a <textarea> and interactive buttons inside <canvas content="drawable" layoutsubtree>.
  2. One ElementGL context with premultiplied uploads and mipmaps. Sets UNPACK_PREMULTIPLY_ALPHA_WEBGL to true, calls stage.begin() before stage.upload() inside paint, and builds trilinear anisotropic mipmaps after texElementSubImage2D().
  3. Deep space starfield and anti-shimmer horizon fade shader. Pass 0 draws layered stars and nebula haze; Pass 1 samples the mipmapped DOM texture with distance LOD softening and a smooth screen-space fade near the top horizon.
  4. True 3D camera, tilt and scroll travel matrix. Builds the 4x4 uMvp matrix mapping unit DOM UVs onto the tilted receding plane across 0° to 68° and 0% to 100% progress.
  5. Calibrated projective updateElementGeometry(). Maps element CSS pixels through the same perspective matrix, scales by geometryUnit() and toggles dataset.hitTick so tilted buttons and fields stay clickable.
  6. Five-argument drawElementImage() trapezoid 2D fallback. When WebGL 2 is absent, draws horizontal clipped strips scaled by perspective depth over a 2D starfield.

How it works

  • One ElementGL context draws two passes on each frame. Pass 0 renders a procedural starfield and subtle nebula haze on a full-canvas quad. Pass 1 draws #crawl-article using a 4x4 perspective matrix uMvp computed from the tilt angle (0° to 68°) and scroll progress (0% to 100%).
  • #crawl-article only uploads on paint events when its DOM content changes (initial load, typing in the heading or textarea, or clicking a button that updates the badge). While scrolling at 60 fps, each frame only updates uniforms and the 4x4 matrix with zero texture re-uploads.
  • Because Chromium's texElementSubImage2D() uploads straight-alpha RGBA when UNPACK_PREMULTIPLY_ALPHA_WEBGL is left at false, the script sets gl.pixelStorei(gl.UNPACK_PREMULTIPLY_ALPHA_WEBGL, true) on context creation and restore so anti-aliased yellow text on a transparent article background blends over dark space without grey fringing.
  • Right after stage.upload(articleEl), the page enables LINEAR_MIPMAP_LINEAR, up to 8x EXT_texture_filter_anisotropic, and calls gl.generateMipmap(gl.TEXTURE_2D) so shrinking lines near the top vanishing horizon stay smooth instead of shimmering.
  • syncHitGeometry() sends the matching 4x4 projective DOMMatrix (scaled by geometryUnit()) to canvas.updateElementGeometry() and flips dataset.hitTick whenever the plane moves or before pointer presses.

Live checks

Each check builds an isolated fixture on testStage() so the live crawl above isn't disturbed.

ResultExperimentDetail

Findings

Measured in headless Google Chrome 160.0.8188.0 canary on 2026-11-27 at 412 px and 2.625 DPR (SwiftShader WebGL). Chrome 157, Playwright check:jank and Chrome 159 on Android stay not verified.

  • Works: mipmapped texElementSubImage2D() without per-frame uploads. Enabling LINEAR_MIPMAP_LINEAR and EXT_texture_filter_anisotropic on the texture returned by ElementGL.upload() with UNPACK_PREMULTIPLY_ALPHA_WEBGL = true renders anti-aliased yellow text smoothly into the deep space horizon, and mipmaps only rebuild when edits fire paint.
  • Works: keeping all points in front of the near plane. Choosing a 4.9-unit camera distance and adapting sTop smoothly between flat 0° and tilted 55° keeps homogeneous w > 1.4 across the entire tall article at every slider extreme, preventing behind-camera clipping in both GLSL and DOMMatrix.
  • Works: projective updateElementGeometry() on tilted controls. Scaling the ndcToCss * VP * uvToWorld * pxToUv matrix by geometryUnit() aligns elementsFromPoint() with buttons inside the crawl at both 0° flat and 50°–55° tilted planes.
  • Limit in the 2D fallback: drawing 26 clipped horizontal strips with 5-argument drawElementImage() creates a receding trapezoid silhouette without WebGL 2, but affine strip scaling leaves visible slice seams across large display headings and borders because 2D canvas can't interpolate 1/w inside a strip.
  • Not verified on real mobile hardware: touch-tapping tilted buttons while crawling at 412 px and 2.625 DPR on Chrome 159 for Android, on-screen keyboard opening inside a tilted <textarea>, and real GPU frame rates.
